title: Biefeld-Brown vacuum tests: 1990 Air Force and 1956 Paris

tellings.quote: For example, in 1990, the Air Force tested a Biffield Brown experiment in a vacuum, but they only used 19 kovts instead of the mega voltage Brown was using.

plain: Michels says that in 1990 the Air Force tested the Biefeld-Brown effect, a claimed thrust from high-voltage electrical devices named after the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, inside a vacuum, but used only 19 kilovolts instead of the far higher voltages Brown had used. He tells it himself, in an episode where the researcher Jacques Cornillon is cited, and contrasts it with Brown's own vacuum tests in Paris in 1956. His point is that the Air Force test was too weak to rule the effect out.
